en:My name is Lin, and I am a computer science student. I chose this subject because I enjoy solving problems. At university, I study programming, databases, and computer networks. Some courses are difficult, so I often discuss them with my classmates. Explaining an idea to someone else helps me understand it better.

en:This semester, I am building a small website with two friends. It helps students find a quiet place to study. I work on the pages that users see, and my friends work on the data. The website is not finished yet. Our next step is to ask five students to try it and tell us what is confusing.
en:I study computer science. I chose it because I enjoy solving problems. This semester, I am building a small website with my classmates.
en:I chose computer science because I like building useful things.

en:On weekdays, Maya has classes in the morning. After lunch, she spends an hour in the library. She does not always finish every task, but she writes down the most important one before she starts. This small habit helps her focus. When she gets stuck, she takes a short walk instead of looking at her phone.

en:In the evening, Maya practises English for fifteen minutes. First, she reads a short text. Then she closes it and explains the main idea aloud. She records her answer and listens once. She chooses just one thing to improve the next day. On Saturdays, she meets a friend to study. Sunday is her day off.
en:I have classes in the morning. After lunch, I study in the library. In the evening, I read a short English text and explain it aloud.
en:First, I read a short text. Then I explain it in my own words.

en:A README is usually the first document you see in a software project. It explains what the project does and how to start it. Before copying a command, check the requirements. A project may need a particular version of Node.js or a package manager. If your version is different, the same command may produce a different result.
